sections.h2: Which offices in Stanton deal with a Powell County tax account?
sections.html:
Three counters in Stanton cover nearly every question a Powell County owner will have. The PVA puts a value on each parcel. The sheriff collects the money. The county clerk holds deeds and the lien paperwork. Rates are voted elsewhere, by the fiscal court, the school board and the library, extension and health districts that appear on a bill.

Powell County, KY: who to call about a tax account
OfficePhoneHandles
Property Valuation Administrator(606) 663-4184Values, exemptions, vehicle assessments
Sheriff(606) 663-2226Bills and payments through April 15
County Clerk(606) 663-6444Delinquent bills, deeds, lien records

The PVA sits at 525 Washington Street, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 277, Stanton, KY 40380, and a fax line at (606) 663-0947. The county publishes the details on its PVA page. Call before visiting, since hours at the sheriff's office and the clerk's office vary by weekday.

sections.h2: How does the PVA arrive at a figure for a Powell County house?
sections.html:
The office appraises each parcel at fair market value for January 1 and states openly that it never decides what you owe, since the bill multiplies that value by rates other bodies adopt. Cars and trucks get the same January 1 treatment. Staff start from NADA guides and can lower a figure for high mileage or for two written repair estimates from licensed body shops.

Owners are not obliged to relist land each spring when last year's roll described it correctly and nothing major changed. After a purchase, the price on the deed can serve as the listed value the following January 1. For Powell County buyers that means a recent sale price often becomes the next assessment.

Business equipment and other personal property goes on a list filed with the PVA between January 1 and May 15, and anything missed by May 15 is treated as omitted and billed later.

sections.h2: What dates govern Powell County bill payment?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 sets the usual calendar for the whole state, and the sheriff collects:

  • Settle everything by November 1 and 2 percent comes off.
  • From November 2 into December, the printed amount applies.
  • January adds 5 percent.
  • February and later add 10 percent, and the Department of Revenue's examples show a sheriff's fee on top.

When mailing slips, the Department can switch to a shifted calendar that gives each stage one month from the mailing date. Which version applies in a given year is printed on the bill, and the sheriff at (606) 663-2226 can confirm it. Once April 15 passes, the sheriff hands whatever remains to the clerk, who records a lien.

sections.h2: What might a Powell County owner actually pay?
sections.html:
For 2025 the state rate fell to 10.6 cents per hundred dollars of assessment, a drop from 10.9 cents in 2024. Census QuickFacts reports a typical Powell County home at $141,100, and the state's slice of that is close to $149.57. County, school and district levies come on top, so only the address-specific bill gives the final total.

Older and disabled owners who qualify for the homestead deduction are taxed on less. Removing $49,100 from $141,100 leaves $92,000, and the state slice shrinks to about $97.52. Early payment trims a further 2 percent.

At a sale, the bill follows the person who held title when the year began. Put the split of the year's bill into the contract, and ask the sheriff for a payoff number ahead of closing.

sections.h2: Can a Powell County owner push back on a value?
sections.html:
Yes, but the sequence matters. Meet the PVA or a deputy first, because the board turns away any case that skipped that step. The tax roll lies open for inspection for thirteen days starting on May's first Monday, Saturdays included, and a higher assessment must come with written notice under KRS 132.450.

  • At the meeting the PVA explains the method and writes down your claimed number.
  • The written appeal goes to the clerk on the workday right after the inspection window shuts.
  • Hearings begin about a month after inspection and can run up to five days.
  • Bring proof: building and land details, insurance policies, construction cost, sales listings. No proof means a denial.

A paid advocate must belong to a listed profession, such as lawyer, CPA, licensed broker or certified appraiser, and carry your signed authorization. Should the board land above your claim after bills are printed, a supplemental bill covers the gap.

sections.h2: Who gets the older owner deduction in Powell County?
sections.html:
The state fixed the deduction at $49,100 for assessments in 2025 and 2026. Seniors from age 65 and people classed as totally disabled receive it on the house they occupy. File at the PVA office on Washington Street and bring a document that proves your age.

A couple gets one deduction, and either spouse turning 65 is enough. After approval, an age-based claim rolls forward while the same person lives there. Disability claims are renewed every year, with exceptions for veterans whose disability is service-connected and for people with a permanent finding from a federal or state retirement program.

The benefit belongs to the person, so a buyer must file again after a sale.

sections.h2: What if taxes on a Powell County house are never paid?
sections.html:
Transferring the deed does not erase them. Under Kentucky law the tax is a personal debt of the owner from the assessment date, and the lien described in KRS 134.420 lasts eleven years whoever takes title next. A title search will find it.

After April 15, 1 percent a month starts, and the state's worked example shows a $1,000 bill turning into $1,254 at transfer, then $1,387.79 inside five business days and $1,611.30 after the first county attorney notice. A clerk's sale follows roughly three to four and a half months after transfer, and whoever buys the certificate gains a lien carrying its own interest and costs. A payment to the sheriff ahead of mid April sidesteps every one of these costs.

sections.h2: How does Powell County's housing market look to a seller?
sections.html:
Carved in 1852 from Clark, Estill and Montgomery land, Powell County has Stanton as its seat and Clay City as its only other town. About 179 square miles of foothills, rising from 580 to 1,440 feet, hold part of the Daniel Boone National Forest. Natural Bridge State Resort Park, the Red River Gorge and the Nada Tunnel bring walkers and climbers, and the county advertises quick access to two interstate highways.

Census QuickFacts supplies the numbers behind the market:

  • July 2025 population estimate of 12,812, which is 2.4 percent below the 2020 base.
  • Owners occupy 68.2 percent of housing units, spread over 4,790 households with 2.65 residents each.
  • Typical home value $141,100, typical rent $747.
  • Household income of $40,309 at the midpoint, with 20.8 percent below the poverty line.
  • Five building permits in 2025, so nearly all sales involve existing houses.

Montgomery, Menifee, Wolfe, Lee, Estill and Clark counties border it. Workers commute 26.6 minutes on average. A house that needs work or carries back tax can still move quickly through a direct cash purchase, with the bill paid at the closing table.

faqs.q: Where does a Powell County tax payment go?
faqs.a: The sheriff, reachable at (606) 663-2226. The PVA, at (606) 663-4184, only assigns values and neither bills nor collects.

faqs.q: What does early payment save on a Powell County bill?
faqs.a: Two percent when the whole amount arrives by November 1 on the regular calendar. A shifted calendar gives one month from the mailing date.

faqs.q: How much is the older homeowner deduction in Powell County?
faqs.a: $49,100 for assessments in 2025 and 2026, subtracted from the home's value for owners at 65 and up or those totally disabled. The PVA supplies the form.

faqs.q: Can I go straight to the appeals board?
faqs.a: No. A meeting at the PVA office must come first. The appeal is then filed with the county clerk on the workday after inspection ends.

faqs.q: If I sell, do old Powell County taxes transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: Delinquent amounts can. A lien lasting up to eleven years stays on the parcel, so the closing statement should pay off whatever is open.
